However, examining `parallel_scan_cuda`, the only kernel launch is: `row_scan_kernel<float><<<outer_elements, threads, shared_mem_size>>>(...)`. The `inclusive_scan_kernel` is defined but NEVER called from any code path. It is dead code.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation occurs in the `inclusive_scan_kernel` function which is completely dead code - it is defined in the CUDA source but never invoked by any caller. The host function `parallel_scan_cuda` only launches `row_scan_kernel`, which uses `threadIdx.x` and remains unchanged between original and mutant. Since the mutated kernel is never executed regardless of input values, shapes, or any other parameter, no input can possibly trigger different behavior. The 112 rounds of differential testing correctly showed bitwise identical outputs because both versions execute the exact same code path.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable - the mutated code is in `inclusive_scan_kernel` which is dead code (never called). The only executed kernel is `row_scan_kernel` which is identical in both versions. No input value strategy can force execution of dead code.
rounds.recommendations: When performing mutation testing on CUDA kernels, first verify that the mutated kernel function is actually reachable from the host entry point. Dead code (unreferenced kernel functions) should be flagged during static analysis to avoid wasting testing resources. Consider adding static reachability analysis to the EMD pipeline to identify mutations in unreachable code paths.
